plan:
Use search_files with keywords like "DM", "agent", "message", "handler", "command" to locate the files that process user chat messages and route intents.

Use read_files and list_functions on the identified files to find the main message‑handling function and any existing command/intent registry (e.g., a map of commands to handlers).

Use semantic_search with phrases like "!hello", "greeting", "simple command" to check if a hello command already exists (to avoid duplication).

Use file_concepts and function_contract on the message‑routing function to understand how new commands are registered and what parameters the handler receives (e.g., user ID, channel, message text).

Use write_file to add a new handler function (e.g., handle_hello) in an appropriate location (or modify an existing command module) that returns or sends the string "hello" as a response.

Use write_file to register the new handler in the command map, associating it with a trigger like "!hello" or "hello".

Use test_coverage to identify existing test files for the DM agent, then use deepseek_consult to generate a simple test that sends a "!hello" message and verifies the response is "hello".

Use write_file to add the generated test to the appropriate test suite.

Use create_branch to create a new branch (e.g., feature/hello-command) for these changes.

Use commit_changes to commit the code and test changes with a descriptive message (e.g., "Add !hello command").
